1.note: The words of 1 Chr 16:32 ("Let the field exult, and all that is in it"; Ps 96:12 has a slightly different wording). Each word is printed with abbreviation marks, which suggests that its letters were read as the initials of a holy Name; the Name is not identified.

2.note: So printed (checked against the scan). Read as חידוש גדול, "a great wonder"; not certain. Note also that R. Moses is called "of blessed memory" at the opening of the paragraph but "may God keep him" in its course; the editor was probably writing after his death from an earlier account.

3.note: 5603 was a leap year with two months of Adar. 9 Adar I 5603 = Thursday 9 February 1843; 9 Adar II = Saturday 11 March 1843. The text does not say which. Sephardi custom keeps the yahrzeit of someone who died in a common year's Adar in Adar II, which would point to 11 March, but this is not certain.

4.note: The abbreviation הפ' is not resolved. Read as הפמליא ("the [heavenly] household", the angels), who were jealous of the young man's holiness; not certain.

5.note: Literally "Rav Ḥaviva", the name of a Talmudic sage, used here as a play: "a beloved rabbi". The abbreviation marks suggest that it also hides his initials (as רב אחי"ם does, for Abraham Ḥai Musafia), but the reading is not clear.

6.note: ע"ס read as על סגנון or על סדר, "in the manner (or: order) of" the Ḥida's printed book of sermons Ahavat David; not certain. In this paragraph only the titles that are plain Hebrew phrases are translated; Sever Yosef and Ḥomat Anakh are left as names. The father's name here is "R. Isaac"; paragraph 134 gives it in full as Raphael Isaac Zeraḥiah (called Zeraḥiah in paragraph 127).

7.he: ג' חצאי פאבל"י ... מעט יותר מה' קראנטאני
7.note: פאבל"י: Italian paoli, silver coins of Tuscany and the Papal States. קראנטאני: carantani, the Italian name of the Austrian kreuzer, current in northern Italy in the nineteenth century. It is not clear whether "a little more than five carantani" is the value of each half-paolo or of all three.

8.note: Probably eighteen chapters of Mishnah, which are customarily studied for the soul of the dead (משנה having the letters of נשמה). The text does not say of what.

9.note: מ"א here is read as מר אביו, "his father", that is, the Ḥida, father of R. Isaiah. Elsewhere in these stories, told in R. Moses' words, מ"א means "my father" (R. Isaiah), which does not fit here, since R. Isaiah is the dreamer.

10.note: א"ח read as Abraham Ḥai. The word טוב ("good") after it is not clear: perhaps part of his name, perhaps a play ("a good brother", אח טוב); left out of the English.

11.note: The gematria is right: יחיה (10+8+10+5 = 33) + האדם (5+1+4+40 = 50) = 83. וס"י read as וסימן, perhaps וסימן יפה, "and a fine sign"; not certain.

12.note: בד"ק read as בדבריו הקדושים, "in his holy words"; perhaps בדף קמא, "on the first page". Not certain.
